reasons: The cited § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment expressly 'without reduction or termination rights', which is the rule's stated walk-away scenario and fails the fallback (12-month term, 30-day reducibility, true-up rather than penalty) on every material term, so 'deviation' is correctly classified.

The redline is directionally correct and actionable: it removes the commitment and states Fees are owed only for Services ordered under an Order Form or actually used, which lands on the preferred position and is internally consistent with §§ 7.1, 9.4 and 12.3 as cited.

The failed minimal-edit check is not disqualifying here — the redline guidance calls for deleting or narrowing the commitment, and a single-sentence take-or-pay clause cannot be fixed without replacing the sentence; no collateral text was touched.
The comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 12-month reducible commitment with true-up as a fallback, matching tone requirements.
